idiom_name: java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantReadWriteLock / StampedLock on the JVM (Scala's synchronized is exclusive)
implementation_notes: Scala has no reader-writer lock of its own: synchronized and @volatile are JVM monitors (exclusive), so read-mostly JVM state is guarded with java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantReadWriteLock or StampedLock, wrapped in the same try/finally discipline. Effect-based stacks (cats-effect, ZIO) instead model shared mutable state as a Ref/AtomicReference with lock-free reads and atomic updates, plus a Semaphore for exclusive sections - the reader-writer distinction usually disappears into immutable snapshots. Keep the classic lock where a Future/thread-based service guards an in-process read-mostly cache and blocking a pool thread is acceptable.
pitfalls: Blocking on a read/write lock inside a Future body occupies a pool thread; the global ExecutionContext can starve (wrap genuinely blocking calls in blocking { } only).
A var read under a read lock still needs safe publication (@volatile or the lock) for fields written by the writer; the lock is not a substitute for the JVM memory model on unguarded reads.
Read-to-write upgrade deadlocks exactly as in Java; release and retry.
In cats-effect/ZIO code never block inside the effect: use Ref/Semaphore instead of a JVM lock.
